deep.reconstruction:
This page opens §5, 'Classes remarquables d'opérateurs dans l'espace de Hilbert'. Grothendieck announces an exposition of Schatten's theory of operator ideals. He says it will be given in a form simplified by a result of Weyl, most likely Weyl's inequalities or majorization for singular values; the previous page, Th. 4 and its corollaries, proves the triangle inequality for unitarily invariant norms from such majorization. He will add some complements.

Definition 1. A norm N on R^n is a 'Schatten norm' if three conditions hold:
- it is symmetric (invariant under permutations of coordinates);
- it is absolute: N(x) = N(|x_1|,...,|x_n|);
- it is increasing on the positive orthant and normalized by N(1,0,...,0) = 1.

In modern terms this is a normalized symmetric gauge function in von Neumann's sense (1937). A norm on R^(N), the finitely supported sequences, is a Schatten norm if it induces one on every R^n, with R^n identified with the sequences vanishing after rank n. A Schatten norm on R^n induces one on every R^m with m ≤ n. The examples are the l^p norms (1 ≤ p < ∞) and the sup norm.

The page then begins a construction. Given a Schatten norm N_0 on R^n, there is a smallest Schatten norm N on R^(N) extending it. For x in c_0, let ρ_i(x) be the decreasing rearrangement of the |x_i|, and set N(x) = N_0(ρ_1(x),...,ρ_n(x)), a Ky Fan-type 'top-n' truncation.

On the next page Grothendieck proves the triangle inequality for this N. He identifies x with a diagonal operator u_x on l^2, whose singular values are the ρ_i(x). He then applies the corollary of Th. 4 (the operator triangle inequality ||u+v||_N ≤ ||u||_N + ||v||_N) to u_{x+y} = u_x + u_y. After that he passes to Köthe-type sequence spaces l^N, defined by N(x) = lim_n N(|x|_n).

Purpose: to set up the correspondence between symmetric sequence norms and unitarily invariant operator ideals (the Schatten–von Neumann classes), for use in Grothendieck's tensor-product work.
errors: Condition 2 (monotonicity on the positive orthant) is redundant: an absolute norm is automatically monotone (cf. Bauer–Stoer–Witzgall 1961). This is harmless.

Minimality of the extension is asserted but not argued on this page. It is correct: any Schatten extension N' satisfies N'(x) ≥ N'(top-n part of |x|) = N_0(ρ_1(x),...,ρ_n(x)) by monotonicity and symmetry.

ideas.what: Definition of Schatten norm: a symmetric, absolute, monotone, normalized norm on R^n or R^(N)
ideas.modern_name: symmetric gauge function / symmetric (rearrangement-invariant) sequence norm
ideas.usually_credited_to: von Neumann (1937); Schatten (1950, A Theory of Cross-Spaces)
ideas.where_published: possibly related material in Produits tensoriels topologiques (1955), Ch. II, on Schatten classes; unsure of exact form

ideas.what: Smallest symmetric-norm extension from R^n to R^(N) via N_0 applied to the top n entries of the decreasing rearrangement
ideas.modern_name: Ky Fan-type truncated symmetric norm extension
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; Ky Fan (1951), dominance theorem context

ideas.what: Proof of the triangle inequality for sequence norms by passing to diagonal operators and using the operator inequality derived from Weyl-type majorization
ideas.modern_name: von Neumann/Ky Fan correspondence between symmetric gauge functions and unitarily invariant norms

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, standard exposition of symmetric gauge functions and Schatten classes, simplified via Weyl/Ky Fan majorization. All of it is known (von Neumann, Schatten, Ky Fan, Gohberg–Krein), with nothing new beyond pedagogy.
transcription_corrections: The interlinear insertion near 'Weyl' likely reads 'sous une forme simplifiée rendue possible par l'inégalité de Weyl' (the text before 'Weyl' is probably 'inégalité de').
The insertion after 'théorie de Schatten' is uncertain; possibly 'inspirée de son livre' or similar.
'Si N_0 est une norme de Schatten sur R^n, il existe une plus petite norme de Schatten N sur R^(N) prolongeant N_0': 'plus petite' is consistent with the image.
